sentences.en: 33 presidents.
sentences.zh: 33位总统。

sentences.en: I called the president at 4.30 in the morning and he answered.
sentences.zh: 我在清晨4点半给总统打了电话，他接了。

sentences.en: Seven decades in space.
sentences.zh: 在太空的七个十年。

sentences.en: We want to see what's beyond the next star.
sentences.zh: 我们想看看下一颗星星的背后是什么。

sentences.en: A thousand consumer product guides.
sentences.zh: 一千份消费品指南。

sentences.en: Today I am testing seven mattresses.
sentences.zh: 今天我正在测试七张床垫。

sentences.en: 60 super sundaes.
sentences.zh: 60款超级圣代。

sentences.en: They were probably the best team in the league every single year.
sentences.zh: 他们可能每年都是联赛中最出色的球队。

sentences.en: 53,500 puzzles.
I use a different starting word every day.
sentences.zh: 我每天都使用不同的首字母单词。

sentences.en: 25,000 recipes.
And I love a one pan recipe because I don't love washing pans.
sentences.zh: 而且我喜欢一锅端食谱，因为我不喜欢洗锅。

sentences.en: The New York Times, celebrating 175 years of helping you understand the world and make the most of each day.
sentences.zh: 纽约时报，庆祝175周年，助您理解世界并充分利用每一天。

sentences.en: Subscribe now for a special offer at nytimes.com slash subscribe.
sentences.zh: 立即订阅，即可在 nytimes.com slash subscribe 享受特惠。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是来自《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Today.
sentences.zh: 今天。

sentences.en: Ever since the discovery that whales produce songs, scientists have been trying to find a way to decipher their lyrics.
sentences.zh: 自从发现鲸鱼会唱歌以来，科学家们一直在寻找破译它们歌词的方法。

sentences.en: After 60 years, they may have finally done it.
sentences.zh: 经过60年，他们可能终于做到了。

sentences.en: My colleague, Carl Zimmer, explains.
sentences.zh: 我的同事卡尔·齐默将对此进行解读。

sentences.en: It's Friday, May 24th.
sentences.zh: 今天是5月24日，星期五。

sentences.en: Hi, Carl.
sentences.zh: 嗨，卡尔。

sentences.en: Hello.
sentences.zh: 你好。

sentences.en: I have to say, after many years of working with you on everything from the pandemic to...
sentences.zh: 我必须说，在和你共事多年、从大流行到……

sentences.en: CRISPR?
sentences.zh: CRISPR？

sentences.en: CRISPR DNA technology, that it turns out your interests are even more varied than I had thought.
sentences.zh: CRISPR DNA技术之后，我发现你的兴趣比我想象的还要广泛。

sentences.en: And they include whales.
sentences.zh: 其中还包括鲸鱼。

sentences.en: They do indeed.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And why?
sentences.zh: 为什么呢？

sentences.en: I mean, what is it about the whale that captures your imagination?
sentences.zh: 我是说，鲸鱼的什么特质吸引了你的想象力？

sentences.en: I don't think I've ever met anybody who is not fascinated by whales.
sentences.zh: 我想我从来没遇到过对鲸鱼不着迷的人。

sentences.en: I mean, these are mammals like us, and they're swimming around in the water.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它们和我们一样是哺乳动物，却在水里游来游去。

sentences.en: They have brains that are much bigger than ours.
sentences.zh: 它们的大脑比我们大得多。

sentences.en: They can live maybe 200 years.
sentences.zh: 它们的寿命可能长达200年。

sentences.en: These are incredible animals, and animals that we still don't really understand.
sentences.zh: 这些是不可思议的动物，也是我们至今仍未真正了解的动物。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Well, it is this majestic creature that brings us together today, Carl, because you have been reporting on a big breakthrough in our understanding
sentences.zh: 好吧，卡尔，正是这种雄伟的生物让我们今天聚在一起，因为你一直在报道我们对

sentences.en: of how it is that whales communicate.
sentences.zh: 鲸鱼如何交流这一理解上的重大突破。

sentences.en: But I think in order for that breakthrough to make sense, I think we're going to have to start with what we have known up until now about how whales interact.
sentences.zh: 但我觉得为了让这个突破说得通，我们得先从我们迄今为止对鲸鱼互动方式的了解开始讲起。

sentences.en: So tell us about that.
sentences.zh: 所以跟我们讲讲这个吧。

sentences.en: Well, people knew that whales and dolphins traveled together in groups, but up until the 1960s, we didn't really know that whales actually made any sounds at all.
sentences.zh: 好的，人们早就知道鲸鱼和海豚会成群结队地出行，但在20世纪60年代之前，我们并不知道鲸鱼其实会发出任何声音。

sentences.en: It was actually sort of an accident that we came across it.
sentences.zh: 这其实算是一个偶然的发现。

sentences.en: The American military was developing sophisticated microphones to put underwater.
sentences.zh: 当时美国军方正在开发用于水下的复杂麦克风。

sentences.en: They wanted to listen for Russian submarines.
sentences.zh: 他们想要监听俄罗斯的潜艇。

sentences.en: Naturally.
sentences.zh: 理所当然。

sentences.en: As one does.
sentences.zh: 意料之中。

sentences.en: But there was an engineer in Bermuda, and he started hearing some weird stuff.
sentences.zh: 但百慕大有一位工程师，他开始听到一些奇怪的东西。

sentences.en: And he wondered maybe if he was actually listening to whales.
sentences.zh: 他开始纳闷，自己听到的会不会其实是鲸鱼？

sentences.en: What made him wonder if it was whales, of all things?
sentences.zh: 是什么让他觉得偏偏会是鲸鱼呢？

sentences.en: Well, the sound did not sound like something geological.
sentences.zh: 嗯，那个声音听起来不像是某种地质活动。

sentences.en: It didn't sound like some underwater landslide or something like that.
sentences.zh: 听起来不像是水下山体滑坡之类的情况。

sentences.en: This sounded like a living animal making some kind of call.
sentences.zh: 这听起来像是一只活生生的动物在发出某种叫声。

sentences.en: It has these incredible deep tones that rise up into these strange, almost falsetto-type notes.
sentences.zh: 它有着不可思议的低沉音调，一直上升到那些奇怪的、几乎类似假声的音符。

sentences.en: It was incredibly loud, and so it would have to be some really big animal.
sentences.zh: 它的声音大得惊人，所以一定是什么非常巨大的动物。

sentences.en: And so with humpback whales swimming around Bermuda, this engineer thought, well, maybe these are humpback whales.
sentences.zh: 由于座头鲸经常在百慕大游弋，这位工程师便想，也许这就是座头鲸。

sentences.en: And so he gets in touch with a husband and wife team of whale biologists,
sentences.zh: 于是他联系了一对鲸鱼生物学家夫妇，

sentences.en: Roger and Katie Payne, and plays these recordings to them.
sentences.zh: 罗杰和凯蒂·佩恩，并把这些录音放给他们听。

sentences.en: And they're pretty convinced that they're hearing whales too.
sentences.zh: 他们也深信自己听到的确实是鲸鱼的声音。

sentences.en: And then they go on to go out and confirm that by putting microphones in the water, chasing after groups of whales, and confirming, yes, indeed,
sentences.zh: 接着，他们通过在水中放入麦克风、追逐鲸鱼群进行实地确认，最终证实，确实，

sentences.en: that these sounds are coming from these humpback whales.
sentences.zh: 这些声音正是来自这些座头鲸。

sentences.en: So once these scientists confirm in their minds that these are the sounds of a whale, what happens with this discovery?
sentences.zh: 那么，当这些科学家在心中确认这确实是鲸鱼的声音后，这个发现带来了什么？

sentences.en: Well, Roger and Katie Payne and their colleagues are astonished that this species of whale is swimming around singing all the time, for hours on end.
sentences.zh: 罗杰和凯蒂·佩恩以及他们的同事都大为震惊，原来这种鲸鱼一直在游来游去地唱歌，没完没了地唱上好几个小时。

sentences.en: And it's so inspirational to them that they actually helped to produce a record that they released, the Song of the Humpback Whale, in 1970.
sentences.zh: 这给他们带来了极大的触动，以至于他们实际上协助制作并在1970年发行了一张唱片——《座头鲸之歌》。

sentences.en: Huh.
sentences.zh: 哦？

sentences.en: And so this is being sold in record stores, you know, along with Jimi Hendrix and Rolling Stones.
sentences.zh: 这歌当时在唱片店里贩售，你知道的，就跟吉米·亨德里克斯和滚石乐队的唱片摆在一起。

sentences.en: And it is a huge hit.
sentences.zh: 而且它大受欢迎。

sentences.en: Really?
sentences.zh: 真的吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: It sells like two million copies.
sentences.zh: 卖出了大约两百万张。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Well, at the time, it was a huge cultural event, this record.
sentences.zh: 在当时，这张唱片可以说是一个巨大的文化事件。

sentences.en: This became almost like an anthem of the environmental movement.
sentences.zh: 它几乎成了环保运动的赞歌。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: And it led, for whales in particular, to a lot of protections for them.
sentences.zh: 并且，它为鲸鱼赢得了大量的保护措施。

sentences.en: Because now people could appreciate that whales were a lot more marvelous and mysterious than they maybe had appreciated before.
sentences.zh: 因为现在人们开始意识到，鲸鱼远比他们之前想象的要更加奇妙和神秘。

sentences.en: And so you have legislation like the Marine Mammal Act.
sentences.zh: 于是便有了诸如《海洋哺乳动物保护法》之类的立法。

sentences.en: The United States just agrees just to stop killing whales.
sentences.zh: 美国同意彻底停止捕杀鲸鱼。

sentences.en: It stops its whaling industry.
sentences.zh: 它终止了自己的捕鲸产业。

sentences.en: And so you could argue that the discovery of these whale songs in Bermuda
sentences.zh: 所以你可以说，在百慕大发现这些鲸鱼歌声，

sentences.en: led to at least some species of whales escaping extinction.
sentences.zh: 至少让某些种类的鲸鱼逃脱了灭绝的命运。

sentences.en: Well, beyond the cultural impact of this discovery, which is quite meaningful,
sentences.zh: 除了这一极具意义的文化影响之外，

sentences.en: I wonder whether scientists and marine biologists are figuring out what these whale songs are actually communicating.
sentences.zh: 我很好奇科学家和海洋生物学家是否正在弄清楚这些鲸鱼歌声到底在交流什么。

sentences.en: So, the pains create a whole branch of science, the study of whale songs.
sentences.zh: 佩恩夫妇开创了一个全新的科学领域——鲸鱼歌声研究。

sentences.en: It turns out that pretty much every species of whale that we know of
sentences.zh: 事实证明，几乎我们所知的每一种鲸鱼

sentences.en: sings in some way or another.
sentences.zh: 都会以这样或那样的方式唱歌。

sentences.en: And it turns out that within a species, different groups of whales in different parts of the world may sing with a different dialect.
sentences.zh: 而且在同一个物种内部，世界不同地区的鲸鱼群体可能会带有不同的方言口音来唱歌。

sentences.en: But the big question of what these whales are singing, what do these songs mean, that remains elusive into the 21st century.
sentences.zh: 但这些鲸鱼到底在唱什么、这些歌声意味着什么这一重大问题，直到21世纪仍然是个谜。

sentences.en: And things don't really change until scientists decide to take a new look at the problem in a new way.
sentences.zh: 直到科学家们决定用一种全新的视角重新审视这个问题，情况才真正发生改变。

sentences.en: And what is that new way?
sentences.zh: 那会是怎样的新方法呢？

sentences.en: So, in 2020, a group of whale biologists, including Roger Payne, come together with computer scientists from MIT.
sentences.zh: 2020年，一群包括罗杰·佩恩在内的鲸鱼生物学家与麻省理工学院的计算机科学家走到了一起。

sentences.en: Instead of humpback whales, which were the whales where whale songs are first discovered, these scientists decide to study sperm whales in the Caribbean.
sentences.zh: 这些科学家不再研究最初发现鲸鱼歌声的座头鲸，而是决定研究加勒比海的抹香鲸。

sentences.en: And humpback whales and sperm whales have very, very different songs.
sentences.zh: 座头鲸和抹香鲸的歌声有着非常非常大的差异。

sentences.en: So, if you're used to humpback whales with their crazy high and low singing voices...
sentences.zh: 如果你习惯了座头鲸那些疯狂高亢和低沉的歌声……

sentences.en: Right, those best-selling sounds.
sentences.zh: 没错，那些最畅销的声音。

sentences.en: Those rockin' tunes of the humpback whales, that's not what sperm whales do.
sentences.zh: 座头鲸那些摇滚般的曲调，抹香鲸可不这么干。

sentences.en: Sperm whales have a totally different way of communicating with each other.
sentences.zh: 抹香鲸彼此交流的方式完全不同。

sentences.en: And I actually have some recordings that were provided by the scientists who have been doing this research.
sentences.zh: 我其实有一些由进行这项研究的科学家们提供的录音。

sentences.en: And so, we can take a listen to some of them.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们可以听一听其中的一些。

sentences.en: Oh, wow.
sentences.zh: 噢，哇。

sentences.en: It's like a rhythmic clicking.
sentences.zh: 听起来像是有节奏的点击声。

sentences.en: These are a group of sperm whales swimming together
sentences.zh: 这是一群抹香鲸聚在一起

sentences.en: communicating.
sentences.zh: 进行交流。

sentences.en: So, whale biologists knew already that there was some structure to this sound.
sentences.zh: 所以，海洋生物学家早就知道这种声音带有某种结构。

sentences.en: Those clicks that you hear, they come in little pulses.
sentences.zh: 你听到的那些点击声，是一小串一小串发出来的。

sentences.en: And each of those pulses is known as a coda.
sentences.zh: 每一小串都被称为一个“尾音”（coda）。

sentences.en: And whale biologists had given names to these different codas.
sentences.zh: 海洋生物学家给这些不同的尾音起过名字。

sentences.en: So, for example, they call one coda one plus one plus three,
sentences.zh: 例如，他们把其中一个尾音叫做“一加一加三”，

sentences.en: which is basically click, click, click, click, click.
sentences.zh: 基本上就是咔、咔、咔、咔、咔。

sentences.en: Or four plus three, where you have four clicks in a row and a pause and then three clicks in a row.
sentences.zh: 或者“四加三”，也就是连续发出四声点击，停顿一下，接着再连续发出三声点击。

sentences.en: Right, and the question would seem to be, is this decipherable communication or is this just whale gibberish?
sentences.zh: 没错，问题似乎在于，这是可解密的交流，还是仅仅是鲸鱼的胡言乱语？

sentences.en: Well, this is where the computer scientists were able to come in and to help out.
sentences.zh: 这就是计算机科学家能够介入并提供帮助的地方了。

sentences.en: The whale biologists who were listening to the codas from the sperm whales in the Caribbean, they'd identified about 21 types.
sentences.zh: 那些聆听加勒比海抹香鲸尾音的海洋生物学家，已经识别出了大约21种类型。

sentences.en: And then that would seem to be about it.
sentences.zh: 然后这就似乎是全部了。

sentences.en: But then, an MIT computer science graduate student named Pratyusha Sharma was given the job of listening to them again.
sentences.zh: 但后来，麻省理工学院的一名计算机科学研究生普拉蒂乌莎·夏尔马被安排重新聆听这些录音。

sentences.en: And what does she hear?
sentences.zh: 她听到了什么？

sentences.en: In a way, it's not so much what she heard, but what she saw.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，与其说是她听到了什么，不如说是她看到了什么。

sentences.en: Because when scientists record whale songs, you can look at it kind of like if you're looking at an audio recording of your podcast, you will see the little squiggles
sentences.zh: 因为当科学家录制鲸鱼歌声时，你可以这样看：就像你看你的播客音频录音一样，你会看到你声音的那些小波形。

sentences.en: of your voice.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 所以海洋生物学家只是看着屏幕上滚动的鲸鱼歌声波形图，并试图对它们进行比较。

sentences.en: And so whale biologists would just look at that ticker of whale songs going across a screen and try to compare them.
sentences.zh: 而夏尔马说，我不喜欢这样。

sentences.en: And Sharma said, I don't like this.
sentences.zh: 我就是觉得，这不是我查看数据的方式。

sentences.en: I just, this is not how I look at data.
sentences.zh: 于是她决定用不同的方式来可视化这些数据。

sentences.en: And so what she decided to do is she decided to kind of just visualize the data differently.
sentences.zh: 本质上，她把这些图像侧过来放，从而看到了完全崭新的东西。

sentences.en: And essentially, she just kind of flipped these images on their side and saw something totally new.
sentences.zh: 她看到的是，抹香鲸其实唱了大量没人真正听出来的内容。

sentences.en: And what she saw was that sperm whales were singing a whole bunch of things that nobody had actually been hearing.
sentences.zh: 她发现的一点是，你会发现某头鲸鱼会一遍又一遍地重复同一个尾音，但它实际上是在玩弄这个尾音。

sentences.en: One thing that she discovered was that you could have a whale that was producing a coda over and over and over and over but it was actually playing with it.
sentences.zh: 它会把尾音拉长，

sentences.en: It was actually stretching out the coda
sentences.zh: 使其变得稍微长一点、再长一点、再长一点，

sentences.en: so it would get a little bit longer and a little bit longer and a little bit longer
sentences.zh: 然后再变短、变短、变短。

sentences.en: and then get shorter and shorter and shorter again.
sentences.zh: 它们能以一种前所未闻的方式把玩它们的尾音。

sentences.en: They could play with their codas in a way that nobody knew before.
sentences.zh: 她还开始发现，鲸鱼可能会在一个尾音的末尾添加额外的点击声，

sentences.en: And she also started to see that a whale might throw in an extra click at the end of a coda
sentences.zh: 也就是说它会一遍又一遍地重复某个尾音，然后在最后

sentences.en: so it would be repeating a coda over and over again and then boom add an extra one
sentences.zh: 轰地加一个额外的点击。

sentences.en: right at the end.
sentences.zh: 用他们的话说，这是一种“修饰音”。

sentences.en: What they would call an ornamentation.
sentences.zh: 所以现在你又多了一种这些鲸鱼在使用的信号。

sentences.en: So now you have yet another signal that these whales are using.
sentences.zh: 如果我们看看抹香鲸能够发出的不同尾音，我们在加勒比海

sentences.en: And if we just look at what the sperm whales are capable of producing in terms of different codas we go from just 21 types that they had found in the
sentences.zh: 之前发现的仅仅21种类型，一下子增加到了156种。

sentences.en: Caribbean before to 156.
sentences.zh: 因此，科学家们表示，我们现在看到的可能是他们所说的“抹香鲸音素字母表”。

sentences.en: So what the scientists are saying is that what we might be looking at is what they call a sperm whale phonetic alphabet.
sentences.zh: 对，这绝对是个大新闻，因为我们目前唯一确知拥有音素字母表的物种就是我们人类，正是人类。

sentences.en: Yeah that's a pretty big deal because the only species that we know of for sure that has a phonetic alphabet is us is us exactly.
sentences.zh: 我们能够使用语言的原因，在于我们只需对口腔做一些小小的动作，就能发出极其丰富范围的声音。

sentences.en: So the reason that we can use language is because we can make a huge range of sounds by just doing little things with our mouths.
sentences.zh: 嘴唇微小的变化就能改变发音，因此我们能够产生一套音素，然后把这些音组合在一起构成单词。

sentences.en: A little change in our lips can change up to a and so we are able to produce a set of phonetic sounds and we put those sounds together together to make words.
sentences.zh: 所以现在我们有了抹香鲸，它们至少拥有

sentences.en: So now we have sperm whales which have at least
sentences.zh: 150种不同版本的发音，仅仅通过对其现有的发音方式做一点点微调就能做到。

sentences.en: 150 of these different versions of sounds they make just by making little adjustments to the existing way that they make sounds.
sentences.zh: 所以你知道的，你可以为它们的音素字母表制作一张图表，就像制作人类音素字母表的图表一样。

sentences.en: And so you know you can make a chart of their phonetic alphabet just like you make a chart of the human phonetic alphabet.
sentences.zh: 这就引发了一个问题：它们会将音素字母组合成单词吗？
